title: Temporal Dynamics of Metacognitive Experience: A Longitudinal Panel Study of AI Recommendations and Purchase Intentions in the Arab E-Commerce Market
content: Although artificial intelligence (AI) recommendation agents increasingly mediate digital marketplaces, their longitudinal cognitive effects on consumers remain underexamined. This study investigates whether repeated encounters with AI interfaces drive within-person changes in processing fluency and subsequent purchase intentions. A three-wave longitudinal panel of 700 consumers across ten Arab e-commerce markets was analyzed using random-intercept cross-lagged panel models to isolate dynamic metacognitive experiences from stable individual traits. The results demonstrate that within-person increases in organized information presentation and partner-oriented AI roles positively predict subsequent processing fluency, which in turn predicts increased purchase intention. Pooled stationary models supported modest longitudinal mediation, whereas moderation and threshold effects for consumers' AI knowledge were statistically unsupported. These findings indicate that evolving AI recommendation experiences shape purchase inclinations through metacognitive accessibility, proving that clear design and collaborative cues can modestly lower cognitive friction over repeated platform exposures.
